verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              अनुक्तं यदि ते किञ्चिद्वाचा विदुर विद्यते। तन्मे शुश्रूषतो ब्रूहि विचित्राणि हि भाषसे ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said If there is anything you have left unsaid, O Vidura, speak to me who am listening to you. You are speaking of interesting things.

verses.sanskrit:
विदुर उवाच।
              धृतराष्ट्र कुमारो वै यः पुराणः सनातनः। तनत्सुजातः प्रोवाच मृत्युर्नास्तीति भारत ॥२॥
verses.english: Vidura said O Dhritarashtra, the ancient and eternal Rishi Sanat-Sujata, who lived a life of perpetual celibacy, said that there was no death, O Bharata.
verses.bhavadeepa: एवं ब्रह्मविद्याधिकारिविशेषणीभूता साधनसंपत्तिः सम्यगुपपादिता तत्र क्वचित्क्वचित्प्रसंगात् यतो यतो निवर्तत इत्यादिना सङ्क्षेपेण ब्रह्मविद्या सूचिता । तां विस्तरेण श्रोतुकामो धृतराष्ट्र उवाच- अनुक्तमिति । ते त्वया ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: स ते गुह्यान् प्रकाशांश्च सर्वान् हृदयसंश्रयान्। प्रवक्ष्यति महाराज सर्वबुद्धिमतां वरः ॥३॥
verses.english: That chief among intelligent beings will speak to you. O great king, on the subjects thought of by you, whether you have made them known or kept them locked up in your heart.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              किं त्वं न वेद तद्भूयो यन्मे ब्रूयात् सनातनः। त्वमेव विदुर ब्रूहि प्रज्ञाशेषोऽस्ति चेत्तव ॥४॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said Do you not know what that internal being will say to me? You, O Vidura, speak (about these things) if your mind has that limit of wisdom.

verses.sanskrit:
विदुर उवाच।
              शूद्रयोनावहं जातो नातोऽन्यद्वक्तुमुत्सहे। कुमारस्य तु या बुद्धिर्वेद तां शाश्वतीमहम् ॥५॥
verses.english: Vidura said I am born among the Shudra class; for that reason, I do not dare say anything more (than what I have already said); the knowledge of that celebrate being, however, is considered by me as eternal.
verses.bhavadeepa: ते तुभ्यम् । गुह्यान् गोप्यान् योगकलादीन् प्रकाशान् शमादीन् हृदयसंश्रयान् धर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यति॥३॥ वर्णाश्रमक्रममुल्लङ्घ्य ब्रह्मविद्यां नोपदिशेदित्याख्यायिकामुखेनाह - किं त्वमित्यादिना । सनातनापरनामा सनत्सुजातः ॥४॥

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मीं हि योनिमापन्नः सुगुह्यमपि यो वदेत्। न तेन गर्ह्यो देवानां तस्मादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ॥६॥
verses.english: He, born is the Brahmana class, even when speaking of highly mysterious affairs, will not incur the blame of the gods; therefore I am speaking thus to you.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              ब्रवीहि विदुर त्वं मे पुराणं तं सनातनम्। कथमेतेन देहेन स्यादिहैव समागमः ॥७॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said Tell me, O Vidura, how I can with this body of mine meet with that ancient and eternal being in this world.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              चिन्तयामास विदुरस्तमृषिं शंसितव्रतम्। स च तच्चिन्तितं ज्ञात्वा दर्शयामास भारत ॥८॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Then did Vidura think of that Rishi of rigid austerities; he, too, becoming aware of that thought showed himself then, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: स चैनं प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। सुखोपविष्टं विश्रान्तमथैनं विदुरोऽब्रवीत्॥९॥
verses.english: Vidura, too, received him by the rites prescribed by custom; and Vidura addressed him when he (the latter) was seated at his ease and taking rest.

verses.sanskrit: भगवन् संशयः कश्चिद्धृतराष्ट्रस्य मानसः। यो न शक्यो मया वक्तुं त्वमस्मै वक्तुमर्हसि ॥१०॥
verses.english: O Lord, there is certainly a doubt in the mind of Dhritarashtra, which cannot be removed by me; therefore it is fitting that you should speak to him (and remove the doubt).

verses.sanskrit: यं श्रुत्वाऽयं मनुष्येन्द्रः सर्वदुःखातिगो भवेत्। लाभालाभौ प्रियद्वेष्यौ यथैनं न जरान्तकौ॥११॥
verses.english: Hearing which (your speech) this chief among men will be past all misery; so that gain and the reverse of gain, what is agreeable and disagreeable, old age and death, fear and jealously, hunger and thirst, pride and prosperity, disinclination for women, sleep, desire, anger, loss and gain may be borne by him (with ease).

verses.sanskrit: विषहेरन् भयामर्षौ क्षुत्पिपासे मदोद्भवौ। अरतिश्चैव तन्द्री च कामक्रोधौ क्षयोदयौ ॥१२॥
